Theme

Body, health & movement

bless you interjection

also after a sneeze, God bless you

classical

Traupman 94
Plin. NH 28.23, on the custom: cūr sternuentēs salūtāmus?
Traupman p. 99

Salvē!

Other words

  • Salūtem!

    also used · modern · Traupman 94

  • Dī tibi bene faciant! — God bless you (in thanks or good wishes)

    optative subjunctive: “may the gods do well by you” · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 5.7.20; Plaut. Pers. 4.3.18 (Lewis & Short), s.v. bene; Traupman p. 99: tibi dī bene faciant

    Not the reply to a sneeze but a blessing in thanks: Lewis & Short, “may the gods bless you”.

See also sneeze.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 94.
